title: Introduce graceful handoff and server quarantine window for streaming sessions (OpenAI compatibility layer)
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added server-side quarantine and graceful handoff for streaming sessions to improve client disconnect/reconnect behavior and reduce duplicate tool/function invocations.
description:
Context: We continue to see production flakiness when clients disconnect mid-stream and then immediately reconnect or replay requests. That combination can produce duplicate tool calls, inconsistent structured outputs, and noisy traces. This PR implements a server-side 'quarantine' and explicit graceful handoff semantics in the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter to reduce duplicate side effects and make client cancel semantics predictable.

Motivations: 1) Prevent duplicate tool/function invocations during short reconnect windows. 2) Provide a client-observable lifecycle for soft cancels and quarantined sessions so SDKs can make safe retry decisions. 3) Keep the behavior opt-in via config flags for Dedicated/Private installs while enabling sane defaults in Hosted.

Summary of changes: - Introduced new runtime config option stream.lifecycle.server_quarantine_ms (default 12000) that holds a session in quarantine after an ungraceful disconnect. During quarantine the server will: * retain KV cache and resume tokens for the session, * reject new tool/function-call-side-effecting resumes for 2/3 of the quarantine window, permitting idempotent reads only, * emit a new SSE event type "session_quarantine" to clients and monitoring agents. - Added a soft-cancel handshake: clients can send a Cancel-Soft control frame or HTTP header X-Soft-Cancel: true for REST calls. The server responds with a guaranteed grace period acknowledgement event "grace_cancel_ack" and a soft-cancel-token the client may use to reattach without triggering tool side effects. - Implemented an explicit resume token versioning scheme (resume_token_v2) that includes a recoverability flag and last-commit-id to allow safe resumption when toolcalls were in-flight. - OpenAI-compat adapter: preserved existing streaming wire format while adding optional events and headers so existing SDKs continue to work. New semantics are guarded behind the header X-OpenAI-Resume-V2 when the client advertises support. - Auditing and telemetry: new metrics stream.quarantine_entered_total, stream.quarantine_resumed_total, stream.soft_cancel_ack_latency_ms and labels for toolcall_dupe_prevented=true/false. Added tracing span annotations to mark quarantine intervals and toolcall suppression windows. - Fallback behavior: if quarantine window expires without rejoin, session state is evicted according to existing TTL logic; any suppressed toolcalls are then replayable only through explicit idempotent replay endpoints. - Tests and canary: added deterministic unit tests for resume token parsing, e2e integration that simulates flaky disconnects, and a small perf canary that measures median resume latency.

Design decisions and tradeoffs: - Quarantine window chosen conservatively (12s) to balance UX (fast reconnects) vs duplicate suppression. Configurable per-deployment for Dedicated/Private. - We opted for a soft suppression (2/3 of quarantine) rather than hard-blocking to allow operator override in emergencies. - Resume token versioning keeps the server backwards compatible; older clients still get basic resume support.

Commits summary: "feat(stream): add quarantine lifecycle state and resume_token_v2;" "feat(openai-adapter): emit session_quarantine and grace_cancel_ack events;" "chore(config): add stream.lifecycle.server_quarantine_ms with defaults;" "test(stream): flaky disconnect e2e harness and unit tests for token parsing;" "docs: streaming lifecycle and SDK guidance."

Files changed (high level): - runtime/stream/lifecycle.go: implement quarantine state machine and eviction hooks. - runtime/stream/resume_token.go: v2 encoding/decoding and validations. - adapters/openai/stream_adapter.go: wire events and header handling. - sdk/python/redwood/stream_client.py: add soft-cancel helper and resume-v2 opt-in flag. - infra/config/defaults.yaml: expose server_quarantine_ms and quarantine_suppression_ratio. - tests/e2e/stream_flaky_reconnect_test.go: deterministic flakey client simulation. - docs/streaming-lifecycle.md: end-user guidance and SDK migration notes. - observability/metrics/streaming.prom: new metrics and alert suggestions.

Review conversation summary: - Ravi requested stricter validation on resume tokens to reject malformed v2 tokens; implemented and unit-tested in commit 3. - Marta asked for clearer SDK guidance around when toolcalls are suppressed vs allowed; added a Decision table to docs and expanded examples in sdk python. - Jonas raised concern about the default quarantine length impacting ultra-low-latency customers; added a per-tenant override and documented behavior for Dedicated. - One intermittent integration test failed on first CI run (stream_flaky_reconnect_test.go) due to a race in the test harness; the harness was hardened and CI reran successfully.

CI summary: Build: pass. Unit tests: pass. Integration: initially failed (race in test harness), rerun: pass. Lint: pass. E2E canary run: pass (measured median resume latency 95ms on canary infra).

Backwards compatibility: Existing clients that do not advertise X-OpenAI-Resume-V2 continue to receive the same streaming events they see today; they will still benefit from reduced duplicates in many cases because session quarantines are honored server-side, but soft-cancel token semantics require client opt-in.

Migration notes for SDKs: - Python/TS SDKs add helper stream_client.soft_cancel() which wraps sending the control frame and waiting for grace_cancel_ack. - SDKs should set X-OpenAI-Resume-V2 when they implement token-stable commits. - Recommend customers update server_quarantine_ms for Dedicated clusters if they rely on <200ms reconnects.

Observability and alerts: suggested alerts for a sudden spike in stream.quarantine_entered_total (indicates client-side regressions) and long tail in grace_cancel_ack_latency_ms.

Security: resume tokens are HMAC-signed with token version metadata; rotation handled by existing key-rotation flow.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main after approvals from reviewers.

Why this is different from prior work: previous PRs focused on client-side resume mechanics and naive reconnect windows; this change centralizes decisioning server-side with explicit telemetry and a guarded opt-in resume token that materially reduces duplicate tool side effects.

Follow-ups: 1) SDK mass rollout and sample migration PRs (ENG-1498). 2) Add a Dedicated admin UI toggle for per-tenant quarantine_ms (PM-95). 3) Long-term: exploration of server-driven client backoff signals to further reduce churn.
notes: Canary monitored for 48h with no regression signals. Customers on Dedicated were notified via ch-ops ticket and given a toggle for immediate rollback.
